// diagnostic

E0434

A call under `#Policy(failures: .Explicit)` can pass a failure up to its caller and is written without `?` or `?(text)`.

What

A call under `#Policy(failures: .Explicit)` can pass a failure up to its caller and is written without `?` or `?(text)`.

Why

A call that can fail passes its failure up by itself. The policy asks that the text show each such call, so a reader sees every point where the function can stop early.

Fix

Write `?` after the call, or `?(text)` to add a context frame; a call read as a receiver is written `(call()?)`. `jet fmt --explicit-failures` writes every mark.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0434: Tests/UI/failures_explicit_policy.stderr.

Error [jet.FailureMarkRequired]: `parse` can fail, so the call is written with `?`
  --> Tests/UI/failures_explicit_policy.jet:13:11
    |
 13 |     rows: parse(path)
    |           ^^^^^
 Why: `#Policy(failures: .Explicit)` writes `?` at every call that can pass a failure up, so each early exit shows in the text
 Fix: Write `?` after the call, or `?(text)` to add a context frame
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0434

Error [jet.FailureMarkRequired]: `load` can fail, so the call is written with `?`
  --> Tests/UI/failures_explicit_policy.jet:20:22
    |
 20 |     first + second + load(path).rows
    |                      ^^^^
 Why: `#Policy(failures: .Explicit)` writes `?` at every call that can pass a failure up, so each early exit shows in the text
 Fix: Write the call as `(…?)`; a `?` before `.` or `(` would read as `?.` or a context frame
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0434
